svg.title: LES DC-3 flight controls as simulated: wheels, columns and pedals to the ailerons, elevators and rudder, the pedestal trims and their tabs, the flap lever and the tailwheel
svg.desc: Simplified block diagram of the simulated DC-3 flight controls. Down the left, the cockpit controls. The dual control wheels roll the aeroplane by chain and sprocket to cables, heavy in roll with no boost of any kind; the aileron trim knob on the aft face of the pedestal; the dual control columns, joined by a torque tube, pitch it through cables to the elevator torque tube aft; the elevator trim wheel on the left of the pedestal head; the flap lever on the pedestal, UP, NEUTRAL and DOWN, hydraulic; the tailwheel lock lever, pulled to lock, the lock being a key in a slot; the dual adjustable rudder pedals for yaw, which at taxi speed also steer the tailwheel; and the rudder trim knob on the pedestal. Cables run across to the surfaces on the right. The wheel cable divides at a junction so that one aileron goes up as the other comes down. Left aileron: 27 degrees up, 18 down, with a geared tab that moves opposite to the aileron at 0.4 of its angle for aerodynamic boost. Right aileron: the same travel, and its geared tab is also the trim tab, 12 degrees either way from the pedestal knob. Elevators, a pair on one torque tube: 30 degrees up, 20 down, with a trim tab on each, 12 degrees up and 12 down from the trim wheel; cold cables shift the neutral trim by about a degree of tab. Split flaps: 0 to 45 degrees, continuously variable, 14 seconds for full travel, hydraulic, Chapter 9; hold the lever, and NEUTRAL traps the fluid and holds them. Tailwheel: full castering; the pedals steer it below 10 knots, fading to little by 30; the lock engages only within 5 degrees of centre and rolling, is a positive key that steering does not release, and is protected by an aluminium shear pin that gives at 0.45 of the wheel's load, 0.40 in Veteran, never in Tourist, after which the wheel castors free; shimmy above 40 knots unlocked, about 4 hertz, worse with a worn wheel; differential brakes and throttle are the real steering at taxi speed. Taxi assists on the OPTIONS tab: rudder input to differential brakes, fading out from 20 to 30 knots, and to differential throttles below 30 knots, each with a sensitivity slider. Rudder: 29.5 degrees left and right, with a geared tab that is also the trim tab, opposite to the rudder at 0.4 of its angle plus 12 degrees of trim either way from the pedestal knob. A note on the control cables: steel cables through an aluminium fuselage; cold-soaked, the airframe shrinks more than the cables and they go slack, a tab floats in the slack and the neutral trim moves, about a degree of tab on the elevator and a third of that on the rudder at minus 20 degrees C; cable temperature follows the outside air with a six-minute lag, and the STATUS tab shows it and the bias. Not drawn: the aileron cross and wing bellcranks, the elevator torque tube and its down-spring, the elevator spring tabs, and the autopilot servos in the cable runs, which belong to the autopilot chapters. A dot marks lines that are joined. Simplified, as simulated; Chapter 10.
svg.text: CONTROL WHEELS
dual · roll · chain and sprocket to cables
heavy in roll: no boost of any kind
AILERON TRIM
knob on the pedestal's aft face
CONTROL COLUMNS
dual, joined by a torque tube · pitch
cables to the elevator torque tube aft
ELEVATOR TRIM WHEEL
left side of the pedestal head
FLAP LEVER
on the pedestal · UP · NEUTRAL · DOWN
TAILWHEEL LOCK LEVER
pull to lock; the lock is a key in a slot
RUDDER PEDALS
dual, adjustable · yaw
and, at taxi speed, the tailwheel
RUDDER TRIM
knob on the pedestal
one aileron goes up as the other comes down
LEFT AILERON
27° up · 18° down
geared tab: moves opposite, 0.4 of the aileron's angle, for boost
RIGHT AILERON
27° up · 18° down; its geared tab is also the trim tab:
12° either way from the pedestal knob,
on top of what the gearing does
ELEVATORS
a pair on one torque tube · 30° up · 20° down
trim tabs, one on each: 12° up · 12° down, from the wheel;
cold cables shift the neutral trim by about a degree of tab
and the pilot retrims as the aeroplane cold-soaks
SPLIT FLAPS
0 to 45°, continuously variable · 14 s full travel · hydraulic
hold the lever; NEUTRAL traps the fluid and holds them
TAILWHEEL
full castering; the pedals steer it below 10 kt, fading to little by 30
LOCK: engages only within 5° of centre and rolling; a positive key,
steering does not release it. An aluminium shear pin gives at 0.45
of its load, 0.40 in Veteran, never in Tourist; then it castors free
SHIMMY above 40 kt unlocked, about 4 Hz, worse when worn
differential brakes and throttle are the real steering at taxi speed
TAXI ASSISTS · OPTIONS tab
rudder input to differential brakes, fading out from 20 to 30 kt,
and to differential throttles below 30 kt; a sensitivity slider each
RUDDER
29.5° left · 29.5° right
geared tab, also the trim tab: opposite to the rudder at 0.4 of
its angle, plus 12° of trim either way from the pedestal knob
CONTROL CABLES
steel cables through an aluminium fuselage:
cold-soaked, the airframe shrinks more than the
cables and they go slack. A tab floats in the
slack and the neutral trim moves, about a degree
of tab on the elevator and a third of that on the
rudder at -20 °C. Cable temperature follows the
outside air with a six-minute lag; the STATUS tab
shows it and the bias it puts on the trim.
Not drawn: the aileron cross and wing bellcranks,
the elevator torque tube and its down-spring, the
elevator spring tabs, and the autopilot servos in
the cable runs, which belong to the autopilot chapters.
